en: *Praise for the Practice of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi and Rebirth According to the Contemplation Sūtra and Other Texts*,
one fascicle,
composed by the Bhikṣu Sengshandao.
I respectfully submit this to all my spiritual mentors and those who assist in rebirth: you must feel profound shame and remorse.
Śākyamuni Tathāgata is truly our compassionate father and mother.
Through various skillful means, you have inspired in us unsurpassed faith;
furthermore, you have taught various skillful methods and gateways that are not merely one,
solely for the sake of us ordinary beings with inverted views.
If one can practice according to the teachings,
then at every gate one shall see the Buddha and attain birth in the Pure Land.
Furthermore, if one sees or hears of anyone practicing virtue, [one should rejoice].
One should immediately assist them with what is wholesome.
If one sees or hears someone practicing the teaching, one should praise them; likewise, if one hears someone speak of such practice, one should do the same.
One should immediately act in accordance with what one has practiced and follow it accordingly;
if one hears that another person has attained awakening,
one should immediately rejoice in that awakening in accordance with it.
What is the reason for this?
It is because we equally take all Buddhas as our teachers,
and take the Dharma as our mother who gives birth and nurtures us.
Sharing a common affinity is not something external;
one must not disparage the teachings and practices for which others have a karmic connection,
while praising only the essential Dharma for which one has a personal affinity.
This is precisely the destruction of one's own Buddha-eye of the Dharma;
once the Dharma-eye is extinguished,
there is no way to set foot upon the right path to Bodhi.
"How can the gate to the Pure Land be entered?
he lamented in sorrow:
"Born blind, one follows the dictates of karma."
Following one's karma, one falls into a deep pit;
by unleashing the fires of greed and hatred,
one harms both oneself and others.
Long submerged in the ocean of ignorance,
one encounters wood but has no means to grasp it.
Therefore, practitioners must [regard] all objects— whether mundane or supramundane— with equal detachment.
Always give rise to a mind of praise and compliance;
do not harbor thoughts of right and wrong, nor resentment. Why is this so?
In order to guard one's own actions of body, speech,
and mind, fearing that unwholesome karma might arise and lead once again to the cycle of rebirth.
This is no different from what was stated previously.
If one can attain restraint over the three types of action regarding both one's own and others' objects,
thereby enabling them to be purified.
This is precisely the direct cause for birth in the Buddha-land.
A question is asked:
"If it is said that the purity of the three karmas is the very cause for birth in the Pure Land," [then...]
How is it that the performance of karma is called pure?
The answer is:
all unwholesome dharmas.
To completely sever and refrain from all actions of body, speech, and mind— both one's own and those of others—
is called purity. Furthermore,
when one's own or others' body, speech, and mind engage in wholesome deeds, one should immediately give rise to a progressively superior spirit of sympathetic joy (*anumodanā*).
Just as all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have rejoiced, I likewise rejoice.
By means of these roots of goodness, I dedicate them toward rebirth in a pure land.
This is called the direct cause.
Furthermore, if one wishes to be born in the Pure Land,
one must exhort oneself and others to extensively praise the adornments of the two types of retribution— the environment and its inhabitants— of that pure land.
One must also understand the causal origins of entering the Pure Land and the fundamental causes and conditions for departing from the Sahā world.
Those who possess wisdom should know this.
He asked again:
"What is the meaning of 'the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi'?
He replied:
In Sanskrit it is called *pratyutpanna*;
here it is translated as "Constantly Walking.
Alternatively, it is the collective name for practicing physical walking without interruption for seven days or ninety days.
It is called *pratyutpanna* because the three karmas are uninterrupted.
Furthermore, the term *samādhi* is also a word from the Western country [India];
here it is translated as "concentration" (*dìng*).
Immediately following the three preceding karmas,
the mind reaches the state it has induced,
and the realm of the Buddha manifests before one.
When the correct object appears before one,
the body and mind experience inner joy;
therefore, it is called "pleasure."
It is also called "Establishing the Vision of All Buddhas. One should know that through the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*,
one aspires for rebirth in the joy of the [Buddha-lands], where the sufferings and hardships of the three realms and six paths cease, and immeasurable bliss prevails.

Constantly sinking through kalpas since time immemorial, I vow to be reborn there; Everywhere I hear only the sounds of birth and death—this immeasurable bliss of the True Reward Land of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, I vow to be reborn there. Pure, adorned, and unsurpassed—this immeasurable bliss;

to deliver those of the Sahā world, he manifests emanations and enters [the womb], I vow to be reborn there. Attaining Buddhahood through the eight phases to deliver sentient beings—this immeasurable bliss.

Some speak of the two vehicles of humans and devas, vowing to be reborn there; Some speak of the causes for the *nirvāṇa* of Bodhisattvas and immeasurable bliss, whether gradual or sudden, clarifying emptiness and existence while vowing to be reborn there.
When the two obstacles of person and phenomena are both dispelled, those with sharp faculties who experience immeasurable bliss all receive benefit—vow to be reborn there!
Those of dull faculties and no wisdom find it difficult to awaken to immeasurable bliss—vow to be reborn there!
The *Sūtra of the Adornment* (*Āḍānaka-sūtra*) speaks of gradual teaching and the vow for rebirth; through cultivation of merit over ten thousand kalpas, one realizes non-retrogression.
The *Sūtra of Immeasurable Joy* (*Amitābha-vyūha-sūtra*), the *Sūtra of Amitābha*, and others speak of the vow for rebirth; this is the Bodhisattva-piṭaka of sudden teaching.

Through immeasurable joy, by single-mindedly reciting the Buddha's name for one day or seven days, one vows for rebirth; at the moment of death, one shall be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss with immeasurable joy.
Upon entering the Land of Amitābha’s Nirvāṇa, one vows to be reborn there; One immediately attains non-retrogression and realizes the birthlessness of infinite bliss.
The merit of cultivation over ten thousand kalpas is truly difficult to sustain;

If one must wait for the realization of Dharma-patience within this Saha world, And if the six realms persist through kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, Infinite bliss remains but a distant hope—therefore, vow to be reborn there.
Greed and hatred are the very karma of saṃsāra; how could afflictions be the cause of non-arising?
To experience immeasurable bliss, pray for rebirth there, where this fire of greed and hatred burns with suffering. It would be better to enter the Land of Amitābha;

Amitābha experienced immeasurable bliss when he first resolved his mind toward enlightenment in his causal stage, praying for rebirth there while suddenly renouncing his royal throne to seek Bodhi. Immeasurable bliss!
Having shaved off my hair and beard in the presence of Buddha Rāṣṭrapāla, I vowed to be reborn there; leaving home to practice the Way, I was named Dharmākara.
From these forty-eight vows for immeasurable bliss, I vowed to be reborn there. Each and every vow was for the sake of immeasurable bliss for all sentient beings;
adorned with myriad jewels, it is called Sukhāvatī. Vast, broad, and level, it is immeasurable and of immeasurable bliss.

May I attain Bodhi and sit with a focused mind, vowing to be reborn there; may I exhaust the limits of the future to deliver immeasurable sentient beings, my body of infinite bliss and its radiant light illuminating the Dharma-realm—may I vow to be reborn there.
May all places reached by that light receive benefit, my body of infinite bliss and its individual rays of light shining in continuous succession—may I vow to be reborn there.
May it shine upon those who seek and practice the mindfulness of the Buddha, their rebirth there being a state of infinite bliss. May I vow to be reborn there.

I wish to be reborn in the lands of the Buddhas of the ten directions; To dwell in peace in Sukhāvatī is truly sublime—may I be reborn in the joy of Immeasurable Bliss and the joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi.
The compassionate intent of Śākyamuni Tathāgata is profound and immeasurable; My original teacher Śākyamuni cultivated universal practices—may I be reborn in the joy of Immeasurable Bliss.
For long periods and throughout vast eons he delivered sentient beings—may I be reborn in the joy of Immeasurable Bliss.

May all Tathāgatas establish skillful means and vows for rebirth therein; May they likewise be like the Honored Śākyamuni today, whose immeasurable joy consists in preaching the Dharma according to capacities so that all may receive benefit. May they each attain awakening and understanding, entering the true gate;

With immeasurable joy, though the gates differ, through eighty-four thousand vows, may there be rebirth therein. This immeasurable joy is for the purpose of extinguishing the causes and effects of karma born of ignorance.
The sharp sword is the name of Amitābha; by vowing to be reborn there, a single invocation removes all transgressions—immeasurable joy!
Śākyamuni Tathāgata, while on the path of practice, vowed to be reborn there; by suddenly renouncing body and wealth to seek the wondrous Dharma—immeasurable joy!
Throughout small kalpas, great kalpas, and long kalpas, vow to be reborn there; by following the Buddha’s words and vowing to practice—immeasurable joy!

In every thought-moment, practicing the six perfections throughout time, I vow to be born there; With compassion, kindness, joy, and equanimity, transforming immeasurable sentient beings, I vow to be born there;
With my three karmas dedicated exclusively to practice without interruption, I vow to be born there; Vowing to become the Unsurpassed Honored One of Bodhi, I vow to be born there;

Attaining the unsurpassed fruit of Bodhi with immeasurable bliss, I vow to be born there; Manifesting billions of emanation bodies to deliver sentient beings with immeasurable bliss, I vow to be born there.

May I be reborn through the single voice that expounds the Dharma according to the capacities of beings; May I be reborn in the immeasurable bliss of each attaining awakening according to their own realization, and in the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi;

May I be reborn in the immeasurable bliss of following the teachings of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, and in the immeasurable bliss of the many gates of the Buddha’s teaching and its eighty-four thousand vows; It is precisely for the sake of sentient beings whose capacities differ that there is immeasurable bliss.
If you wish to find a dwelling place for your peace of mind, vow to be reborn there. First seek the essential practice to enter the Gate of Truth;
though the gates of immeasurable bliss differ in name, they are the gradual teachings—vow to be reborn there. Through ten thousand kalpas of ascetic practice, one realizes non-arising;

with immeasurable bliss, take the end of life as the limit and single-mindedly recite the Buddha’s name—vow to be reborn there. In an instant, when life is severed, the Buddha will come to welcome you—immeasurable bliss.

If even for the duration of a single meal one harbors the aspiration to be reborn there, how could one not aspire for ten thousand kalpas? How can one who is free from greed and anger seek the immeasurable bliss of greed and anger?
Such attachment obstructs the path to the realms of humans and devas; therefore, I vow to be reborn there. Within the three evil paths and four realms of existence, one dwells in suffering;

desiring to reach Amitābha’s Land of Peaceful Nurturing where there is immeasurable bliss, I vow to be reborn there. One must dedicate the merit of reciting the Buddha’s name and practicing the precepts toward that immeasurable bliss.
With precepts observed with single-minded diligence, may all Buddhas praise me and vow to welcome my rebirth;

at the end of life, may a lotus throne come of its own accord to receive me—may I vow to be born there in immeasurable bliss, entering the Buddha’s assembly in a single thought-moment. May the names of the three realms and six paths be forever eliminated;

may immeasurable bliss prevail where the three knowledges and six supernormal powers are all mastered—may I vow to be born there. Until the end of life, may I never regress and realize the unconditioned; may immeasurable bliss prevail.

May I always see the Buddha in the four modes of deportment and vow to be reborn there; Holding incense and flowers in my hands, may I constantly make offerings with immeasurable joy, and in a single thought-moment, may I listen along with the assembly and vow to be reborn there;

May the hundreds of thousands of samādhis be spontaneously accomplished, and with immeasurable joy, may I always enter meditative concentration at all times and vow to be reborn there; Having established this principle, may I hear the sutras and attain awakening with immeasurable joy.

May I be reborn there, where the adornments of a hundred jewels appear according to one's thoughts; may I repay the immeasurable kindness of the Buddhas through offerings for long kalpas, and may all karmic traces from the past be extinguished through wisdom amidst infinite bliss.

May I be reborn there, where the unawakened mind spontaneously enters the gate of True Suchness, and where the immeasurable bliss of kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—whether great or small *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas—is experienced in the brief interval of a finger-snap. May I be reborn there in this infinite bliss.
I vow to be reborn in such a place of carefree joy; what else could I crave that I would not seek birth there?
Even if one were to experience the five desires for a thousand years, it only increases the causes and conditions for suffering in hell.
If one craves immeasurable bliss while greed, hatred, and the ten evil deeds continue to arise, how could that be the cause for liberation or nirvana? I vow to be reborn in immeasurable bliss.
Fearing not the three miserable realms while committing manifold sins, yet wishing for rebirth—this is immeasurable bliss.
Destroying the Triple Gem and sinking forever into despair, failing to be filial toward one’s parents and reviling one’s kin—this is immeasurable bliss.
Finding no end to one’s stay in hell, having sunk into the sea of suffering since time immemorial, never having heard the essential Dharma of the West—this is immeasurable bliss.
Though you have obtained a human body, many obstacles abound; vow to be reborn in that land of immeasurable bliss. Failing to receive the Buddha’s transformation, you instead give rise to doubt;

the Tathāgatas of the six directions are supremely compassionate—vow to be reborn in that land of immeasurable bliss. With one heart and one mind, exhort others to go to the West; there is immeasurable bliss.

Suffering from chronic illness or traveling afar, do not count the days; vow to be reborn in that land of immeasurable bliss. Mindfulness of the Buddha is itself the Way; it requires no effort—there is immeasurable bliss.
Such people are difficult to transform and deliver; I vow to be reborn there. Enshrouded by ignorance, they sleep forevermore;

I vow to be reborn in the immeasurable bliss of those who single-mindedly recite the *Amitābha Sūtra* and the *Contemplation Sūtra*. Every phrase and every sentence speaks of the immeasurable bliss of the Western Land; I vow to be reborn there.
Countless billions of jeweled banners beneath the earth are perfectly square and radiant with light; I vow to be reborn in that immeasurable bliss.

May I be reborn there, where ten billion jewel orbs reflect and adorn one another; May I be reborn there, where each manifests wondrous and rare phenomena, and immeasurable bliss illuminates the ground adorned with supreme jewels.
May I be reborn there, where variegated colors surpass a hundred thousand suns, and immeasurable bliss shines from my own body in a purple-gold hue.
May I be reborn there, walking slowly as my feet tread upon the jeweled ground, in immeasurable bliss.

May I attain rebirth in this land of the precious realm of non-arising; By the grace of Amitābha’s immeasurable vow-power, may I enjoy infinite bliss and hear the wondrous Dharma at all times—may I attain rebirth.

Without cause for the arising of afflictions or karmic obstructions, may I enjoy infinite bliss with bodhisattvas as spiritual friends and fellow students—may I attain rebirth. Hand in hand, we shall enter the precious hall together, enjoying infinite bliss.

In every thought-moment, receiving the joy of the Dharma, I vow to be born there; In an instant, awakening to hundreds of thousands of gates of immeasurable bliss, the great assembly, with one heart, weary of this realm, vows to be born there;
Riding upon the power of the Buddha’s vow to behold Amitābha and his immeasurable bliss, suddenly reflecting upon this, my heart and marrow ache;
I vow to be born there; Throughout endless kalpas, I have laboriously exhausted myself in vain; now, I seek immeasurable bliss.
I rejoice that in this life I have heard of the Pure Land and vow to be reborn there; Not sparing even body or life, I go to the West, to the immeasurable bliss.

In the West lies joy and the state of non-action; I vow to be reborn there. The heavens and the human realm possess incomparable and immeasurable joy, Yet the six celestial realms, each surpassing the last by billions of times, Do not equal the immeasurable joy of a single mark of a person in the West. I vow to be reborn there.

With the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, may I attain mastery and aspire to be born there; May the radiance of my body illuminate the worlds of the ten directions, and may immeasurable bliss follow from being a sovereign of the world up to the sixth heaven—may I aspire to be born there.

The music surpasses that of billions of others, and in the Buddha-land of immeasurable bliss, the branches of the jewel forests touch one another—may I aspire to be born there. The music of the sixth heaven is not equal to even a single moment of that immeasurable bliss.
Relying on timely offerings, fragrant winds arise; may I vow to be born there. Brushing against the trees, flowers fly down onto the jeweled ground;
there is immeasurable joy. Jewel trees scatter blossoms that float upon the waters of virtue; may I vow to be born there. Young boys seize them and fashion them into boats; there is immeasurable joy.
Boarding these boats, one enters directly into the Lotus Assembly; may I vow to be born there. Transformed Buddhas and Bodhisattvas provide robes and garments; there is immeasurable joy.

Each holding incense and flowers, they stand before the Buddha vowing to be reborn there; slowly scattering them from afar, they transform into clouds of infinite joy and precious adornments that become canopies—vow to be reborn there. They are immediately given precious fruits and instructed to eat them;
encountering infinite joy, they vow to be reborn through meeting a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*). Hearing the name of Amitābha in the Pure Land brings infinite joy.
By the power of the Buddha’s vows, I come to behold you; I pray for rebirth there. Dwelling eternally in this land, there is no need to return;
accompanied by immeasurable joy and dharma-fellows, we enter the grove to gaze upon it—may I be reborn there. The radiance beneath his feet surpasses the sun and moon;
immeasurable joy arises from the boundless assembly of bodhisattvas—may I be reborn there. Each individual’s body-light illuminates one another; immeasurable joy.
May I be reborn there, newly transformed by birth, with a purple-golden body, no different from the great assembly;
may I be reborn there amidst immeasurable bliss, entering a jeweled pavilion to sit among the multitude. May those who see me in the great assembly all rejoice in immeasurable bliss;

may I be reborn there amidst immeasurable bliss, where various adornments are beyond comprehension. May I be reborn there amidst immeasurable bliss, where looking inward and outward is without obstruction.

May I pause for a moment to receive the joy of the Dharma and aspire to be born there; May I spontaneously awaken to the immeasurable bliss of the Samādhi of Non-arising, adorned with various jewels upon the ground, and aspire to be born there;
May I aspire to be born where countless precious thrones and lotus pedestals of myriad colors and forms fill every place, providing immeasurable bliss;
May I aspire to be born where, according to one's heart’s desire, light shines forth to provide immeasurable bliss.

May the assembly of hundreds of thousands of bodhisattva youths vow to be reborn there; each holding incense and flowers, they gaze upon the pond of immeasurable bliss, whether sitting or standing upon its banks and channels—may they vow to be reborn there. Or some ascend the steps and enter the precious pond of immeasurable bliss;
or they stand in the sand up to their knees—may they vow to be reborn there. Or they sink to their waists and heads, or [the water] flows down in cascades of immeasurable bliss.
Some take golden blossoms with leaves of a hundred jewels and vow to be reborn there;
They bestow them upon those on the shore gazing at the pond, receiving immeasurable joy and a myriad kinds of fragrant flowers, and vow to be reborn there;

They immediately scatter them over the great assembly of Amitābha, and the flowers thus scattered become canopies of immeasurable joy; Spontaneous music circles in a thousand layers of immeasurable joy.
The jewel birds sing in unison as they perform celestial music; may I be reborn there. All who see me give rise to a heart of compassion;
with immeasurable joy, I now arrive here through the power of the Buddha’s vows; may I be reborn there. When shall we come together in shared conditions and shared practice?

With immeasurable joy, I universally pray that all my kinsmen and friends in Jambudvīpa may be reborn there. May those who share our practice remain close to one another and never retreat; with immeasurable joy.

Recite exclusively the *Amitābha Sūtra*, the *Contemplation Sūtra*, and other texts, vowing to be reborn there; bow to the Buddha and engage in contemplation, dedicating all of it toward that immeasurable bliss.
At all times, continuously maintain the vow to be reborn there, making it your sole purpose until death.
Once you reach Amitābha’s Land of Peaceful Nurturing, you shall attain immeasurable bliss and ultimately dwell in the liberation of Nirvāṇa. This is immeasurable bliss.

May I be reborn there, where the adornments of Nirvana fill every wish; Seeing forms and smelling fragrances, may my karmic obstructions be cleared away, and with immeasurable joy, may I soar through the air performing divine transformations—may I be reborn there!

Praising the inconceivable purity of that land, with immeasurable joy, or scattering flowers and incense as offerings to the Buddha—may I be reborn there! To repay the Buddha’s compassionate grace with an inexhaustible heart, with immeasurable joy.
Not relying on the power and vows of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, how could one hear of the immeasurable bliss of Amitābha’s Pure Land?
May all sentient beings whose obstacles are exhausted hear this and rejoice, vowing to be reborn there. May they suddenly sever all evils and vow to seek birth in immeasurable bliss.
May they vow to be reborn in the bliss of the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi*. May they vow that in this very life, they will accord with the Buddha’s teachings and abide in immeasurable bliss.

Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, focus single-mindedly on the Buddha and vow to be born in the Pure Land; all wholesome deeds must be dedicated together toward this end—vow to be born in the Pure Land through constant repentance at every moment of infinite bliss.
At the time of death, one shall immediately ascend the Vajra Terrace—vow to be born in the Pure Land through infinite bliss at all times while facing west in prostration.
This expresses the mutual orientation of the minds of ordinary beings and sages—vow to be born in the Pure Land through infinite bliss.

The Buddha knows that the minds of sentient beings are distracted; they aspire to be reborn there, And thus he specifically teaches them to dwell in right mindfulness in the West, a land of immeasurable bliss.
They do not know that the land of Amitābha is neither far nor near; they aspire to be reborn there. The Way of the Buddha surpasses hundreds of billions of lands of immeasurable bliss;
though the distance is vast, it is not difficult to reach. In the space of a finger-snap, one enters the jewel pond, a place of immeasurable bliss.
I only regret that sentient beings doubt whether or not they will be welcomed to be born in the Pure Land;

yet, facing it face-to-face without conflict, its immeasurable bliss is beyond description—may you vow to be born there, regardless of whether Amitābha specifically gathers you in. The intent lies in single-mindedness:

whether one turns back or not, once the heart is turned, the immeasurable bliss is certain—may you vow to be born there, for at the moment of death, the jeweled canopy will come of its own accord to welcome you. Its immeasurable bliss is beyond description.
May I be born in that jewel land by entering through the flower of the Buddha-vehicle; may I behold the great assembly and realize non-arising—may I be born there in immeasurable bliss.

May I enter each jeweled pavilion at will—may I be born there in immeasurable bliss; its inner and outer adornments are beyond comprehension, where birds sing in harmony and bodhisattvas dance—may I be born there in immeasurable bliss.
Where youths joyfully manifest supernatural powers—may I be born there in immeasurable bliss.
May those born here in my Sahā world vow to be reborn there; may they offer various kinds of worship to gladden the Buddhas and experience immeasurable bliss.
May the Buddhas dispatch people to come and behold them, and may they vow to be reborn there. Everywhere there is only inconceivable and immeasurable bliss;
the earth and the void are filled with holy beings—may they vow to be reborn there. Jeweled nets of pearls naturally cover all, and there is immeasurable bliss.
Gentle breezes stir them, producing wondrous sounds; may I be reborn there. Within these sounds, the unconditioned Dharma is proclaimed;

with immeasurable joy, seeing the trees and hearing the waves, one attains the patience of the Dharma—may I be reborn there. Young children hold flowers, surrounding and praising [the Buddha] with immeasurable joy;
standing in attendance upon Amitābha, they listen to the preaching of the Dharma—may I be reborn there. Craving the joy of the Dharma transcends time and eons; it is immeasurable joy.
May I follow the vows of the bodhisattvas of my own land and be reborn there—this realm of unconditioned nirvana and immeasurable bliss.
May I be reborn where the Dharma is heard throughout all Buddha-fields, traveling to other lands to practice offerings and immeasurable bliss.
May I dwell upon a single meal, transcending a thousand kalpas, and be reborn there. May I remember my fellow practitioners here in this Sahā world and enjoy immeasurable bliss.
Even the atoms of the great earth may still be numbered; May I be reborn in the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, which are inexhaustible and immeasurable in their bliss.
Each and every buddha-field is adorned and pure; May I be reborn there, no different from the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
In that immeasurable bliss, all Tathāgatas behold me with joy; May I be reborn there, where the assembly of noble Bodhisattvas goes forth to observe. In that immeasurable bliss.

May all adornments be like those of Sukhāvatī; may I vow to be reborn there. With miraculous transformations and unimpeded supernatural powers, infinite bliss fills the earth and the sounds of the void pervade everywhere;
may I vow to be reborn there. Hearing every resonance and sound, one attains awakening; with the infinite bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, may I vow to be reborn there.
Continuously recollecting the Buddha to repay the kindness of my teacher, may I enjoy infinite bliss.
Though one may give away wealth and property to create merit and vow to be reborn there, it is not as good as upholding the precepts, severing greed and anger, and experiencing immeasurable joy;

universally honoring all sentient beings, constantly recollecting the Buddha, and vowing to be reborn there. One must dedicate the merits of both self and others toward immeasurable joy, settling the mind in tranquility and stability to give rise to peace and bliss, and vow to be reborn there.
Thus, one alone transcends the three realms and escapes the cage of afflictions, attaining immeasurable joy.

At the moment of death, one beholds the Buddha’s lotus pedestal; by making the supreme vow, one aspires to be reborn there. In an instant, one enters the jewel pond assembly and experiences immeasurable bliss;
the multitude of lotuses and the great assembly all rejoice, and with the vow to be reborn there, one immediately receives celestial robes to wear at will and experiences immeasurable bliss.
Bodhisattvas and śrāvakas, about to behold the Buddha, aspire to be reborn there. By performing a single prostration to the Buddha, one attains the bliss of non-arising and immeasurable joy.
Amitābha spoke: "O sons of the Buddha, I pray that you will be reborn in Sukhāvatī. How can the immeasurable bliss of that realm compare to this triple world?
Those who have newly attained birth through transformation all desire to repay their vows; I pray that you will be reborn there. With palms joined, they wept with choked voices, unable to speak:

"We shall obtain immeasurable bliss and escape the long kalpas of suffering in Saṃsāra. We pray that you will be reborn there. "Today we behold the Buddha; the grace of Śākyamuni is immeasurable. (The assembly replied: "Immeasurable bliss!"
The immeasurable joy of aspiring for rebirth through the bliss of the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi*, following the Buddha’s words to behold Amitābha;
The immeasurable joy of universally exhorting fellow practitioners and spiritual friends to aspire for rebirth together, walking the same path with mutual intimacy and never parting;
The immeasurable joy of parents, wives, and children—hundreds, thousands, and tens of millions—aspiring for rebirth together, which is not merely a superior condition for awakening (*bodhi*).

May I be reborn there, so that though my thoughts bind one another as I enter the evil realms, I may experience immeasurable bliss; May I be reborn there, so that though I manifest divided bodies to undergo retribution without mutual knowledge, I may experience immeasurable bliss;
May I be reborn there, so that though I am covered in hair and bear horns among the six domestic animals such as pigs and sheep, I may experience immeasurable bliss;

May I be reborn there, so that having joyfully attained a human body and heard the essential Dharma, I may experience immeasurable bliss; May I be reborn there, so that I may suddenly abandon foreign lands and return to my native country, experiencing immeasurable bliss.
Father and son meet and rejoice exceedingly, vowing to be born there; so too do the Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas.
Immeasurable joy arises as they may wander forth to enter the forests and gaze upon it, vowing to be born there. Seated upon lotus pedestals, they ascend towers to behold it;
immeasurable joy arises as they behold Amitābha’s land of the seven treasures, vowing to be born there. Upon the earth and in the void, radiant lights shine upon one another; immeasurable joy.

May I immediately manifest spiritual powers throughout the Buddha-lands and vow to be reborn there; may I make offerings everywhere to boundless assemblies and experience immeasurable joy, entering each great assembly according to the needs of beings and vowing to be reborn there. May I enter these places and hear only the Dharma of equality and immeasurable joy;
may my four modes of conduct always remain in meditative concentration and vowing to be reborn there. Without emerging from samādhi, may I perform spiritual powers and experience immeasurable joy.

May I attain rebirth by means of each and every supernatural power to reach the Buddha’s assembly; May I attain rebirth in the immeasurable bliss of hearing the Dharma at every assembly and realizing non-arising, and in the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi;

May I attain rebirth in the true peace and security of the body, which is indeed sublime, and in the immeasurable bliss of golden towers, jade pillars, and lapis lazuli palaces; In the immeasurable bliss of true pearl pavilions arranged in hundreds of thousands of rows.
Layer upon layer of jeweled nets reflect one another in adornment; I vow to be reborn there. Jewel cords are interlaced, hanging with tinkling bells;
infinite bliss as fragrant breezes stir at all times—I vow to be reborn there. Within every sound, the names of the Triple Gem are proclaimed;

infinite bliss as the sentient beings of that land possess sharp faculties of mind and eye—I vow to be reborn there. Hearing but once, they awaken to and understand hundreds of thousands of gateways; infinite bliss.

May I be born there through the joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi; may my body dwell everywhere, yet not equal that immeasurable joy shared with all the youths as they play in the void—may I be born there. May I scatter fragrant flowers from my hands as a mental offering of immeasurable joy;
may the radiance of my body and my necklaces stand illuminating one another—may I be born there. All adornments and light are likewise immeasurable joy.
Some play musical instruments as an offering to the Buddha, vowing to be reborn there; The transformed Buddhas, out of compassion, bestow predictions from afar.
May we share immeasurable joy with hundreds of thousands of millions of spiritual friends who vow to be reborn together; Riding upon lotus flowers, they enter directly into the assembly in the void;
Each assembly is distinct, numbering in the billions—may we vow to be reborn there; Passing back and forth between them without obstruction—immeasurable joy.
Constantly preaching the Dharma at all times, may I be reborn there; Seeing and hearing brings joy, and all sins are eliminated—what immeasurable bliss!
The Buddha and the assembly of sages have bodies of golden hue; may I be reborn there. Their radiance shines upon one another, their minds know one another—what immeasurable bliss!
Adorned with the marks and signs of perfection, they are without distinction; may I be reborn there. All are accomplished through the power of Amitābha’s vows—what immeasurable bliss!
May those who fill the earth, the void, and the realms of men aspire to be reborn there;
May they spontaneously know the infinite bliss of supernatural transformations, Or create flower towers and jeweled cloud-canopies, aspiring to be reborn there;

May transformed birds chorus together to play the sounds of the Dharma, With infinite bliss as the Dharma-sounds swirl like gathering clouds, aspiring to be reborn there; When the humans and devas of that land hear them, they immediately awaken to infinite bliss.

I vow to be reborn after one kalpa, many kalpas, or throughout the long duration of kalpas; I vow to be reborn in the inconceivable and immeasurable bliss of receiving only the joy of the Dharma, and in the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi;
I vow to be reborn where the gates of the adornments of Ultimate Bliss are all opened, in that immeasurable joy;
may all those with a karmic affinity who practice together likewise vow to be reborn; Enter directly with a single-minded focus without doubt, in this immeasurable joy.
Upon arriving in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing of Amitābha, I vow to be reborn there;

It is originally the realm of my Dharma King, where brothers share immeasurable joy—may the assembly of Arhats, bound by karmic affinity, vow to be reborn there. The Bodhisattvas are my Dharma companions and spiritual friends, where immeasurable joy is found;
whether walking or sitting, all hear the Dharma—may they vow to be reborn there. Whether going or coming, there is no obstruction, and immeasurable joy prevails.
May I be reborn there—entering the jeweled ponds to bathe my body and crown, Or standing on dry land amidst jeweled sands, rejoicing in immeasurable bliss as gentle ripples produce wondrous sounds;
May I be reborn there—where within those sounds the Dharma of compassion is purely proclaimed, and the waters of immeasurable bliss and virtue flow clear for thousands of miles;
Where the jeweled sands reflect with such clarity that they seem shallow, and immeasurable bliss prevails.
May I be reborn there, where the four shores are adorned with the seven treasures interspersed;
Where the bottom is spread with golden sand in hundreds of thousands of colors, and immeasurable joys arise from each distinct hue as they radiate brilliant light.

May I be reborn there, where jeweled trees fly down blossoms into the water, and immeasurable joys arise as the branches of every tree hang down like precious canopies. Surrounding it for three hundred thousand *yojanas*, there is immeasurable joy.
May I be reborn there, where roots, stems, branches, and leaves are interspersed with the seven treasures;
May I be reborn there, where each jewel radiates countless lights and immeasurable bliss as gentle breezes arise and cause them to touch one another;

May I be reborn there, where the music of the six heavens cannot compare to its immeasurable joy, and where transformation Buddhas and Bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges dwell; May I be reborn there, where beneath every tree one hears the true sound and experiences immeasurable bliss.

I vow to be reborn in the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi; Once entered, never regressing until reaching Bodhi—may I be reborn in this immeasurable bliss, a vast and level ground of myriad jewels. From each jewel issue hundreds of thousands of lights—immeasurable bliss;
Each light forms a jeweled terrace and seat—may I be reborn there. The lights transform into towers numbering hundreds of billions—immeasurable bliss.

May the countless youths of the Transformation Heaven all aspire to be born there; All are those who, through mindfulness of the Buddha, attain birth in that land of immeasurable bliss, where they sport within jeweled towers and palaces.
May they aspire to be born there, free from hunger and thirst, abiding in profound and eternal immeasurable bliss;
Or may they enter the Hall of Radiance Adorned with a Hundred Jewels and aspire to be born there; Precisely meeting the great assembly to praise Amitābha, they enjoy immeasurable bliss.

Some pray for rebirth, aspiring from now until the fruit of Buddhahood; Praising the Buddha through long kalpas to repay his immeasurable kindness, yet failing to receive the bliss of Amitābha’s great vow, they pray for rebirth. At what time, in what kalpa, shall one leave Saṃsāra?
Having arrived at that place of immeasurable bliss, may one enjoy the Dharma-bliss; May one ultimately never hear the sound of the ten evil deeds—this is immeasurable bliss.

Having seen the Tathāgata with my eyes and heard the Dharma with my ears, I vow to be reborn there; My body has always followed the Buddha, experiencing immeasurable joy and compassion—how could I have expected such bliss to arrive today?
I vow to be reborn in the Land of Jewels; This is truly the power of the Original Teacher of this Sahā world, bringing immeasurable bliss;
had it not been for the exhortation of the Original Teacher and my spiritual friends, how could I have entered the immeasurable bliss of Amitābha’s Pure Land? I vow to be reborn there.
The immeasurable joy of aspiring for rebirth through the bliss of the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi*; The immeasurable joy of being reborn in the Pure Land to repay the infinite kindness of one's teacher;
I universally exhort all those with affinity, whether monastics or laypeople, to aspire for rebirth; The immeasurable joy of single-mindedly practicing the Buddha’s teachings at this assembly;

The immeasurable joy of reciting the sutras with focused mindfulness while contemplating [the Buddha], and aspiring for rebirth; The immeasurable joy of worship, praise, and adornment, free from distraction or confusion.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, may my mind remain continuous in the vow to be reborn there; may the adornments of Sukhāvatī be spontaneously seen and immeasurable bliss attained.
Whether through visualization or contemplation, may the obstacles of karma be removed and the vow for rebirth fulfilled; all this is through the power of Amitābha’s original vows.

Through the Buddha’s power, immeasurable bliss is realized as samādhi, and the vow for rebirth is fulfilled; once samādhi is attained, the eye of the mind opens, and immeasurable bliss is experienced.

The realm of all Buddhas transcends that of ordinary beings; I vow to be reborn there. Knowing only how to feel shame and gratitude for the immeasurable kindness of Śākyamuni, I vow to be reborn there.
The Tathāgatas of the ten directions extend their tongues to bear witness to my vow for rebirth;

It is definitively judged that one will attain rebirth in the nine grades and return to immeasurable bliss, Where father and son welcome one another into the great assembly, and one immediately inquires about the bitter sufferings of the six realms—this is immeasurable bliss. I vow to be reborn there.
Some obtain the retribution of humans and devas and vow to be reborn in [the Land of] Immeasurable Bliss;

At that time, seeing those suffering from hunger and exhaustion with sores breaking out upon their bodies, Amitābha and the great assembly vow to be reborn there. Hearing your description of these sufferings, they all lament in sorrow; Amitābha speaks, saying:
"O sons of the Buddha, vow to be reborn in [the Land of] Immeasurable Bliss! You shall receive the fruits of your own actions; do not resent others! [The Land of] Immeasurable Bliss.

I vow to be reborn in the joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi; I vow to be reborn in the eternally abiding precious land, forever free from sorrow, filled with immeasurable bliss, the state of nirvana’s happiness and non-action. In the burning house of greed and hatred, such immeasurable bliss has never been heard of;
I vow to be reborn there to sit at will upon pedestals of immeasurable jewels and flowers. Seated there, the assembly of sages is infinite and beyond measure—immeasurable bliss!

The youth makes offerings to the śrāvakas and prays for rebirth—what immeasurable joy! Birds delight in flying through the air, circling hundreds of thousands of times in a mere moment while sitting or standing—what immeasurable joy!
All past karma, as numerous as motes of dust, is utterly eliminated—what immeasurable joy!
Or celestial garments are scattered, covering the jeweled ponds—what immeasurable joy! Upon those garments, precious flowers and incense are further scattered—what immeasurable joy!
When the Holy Assembly walks, their feet tread upon the ground; may I be reborn there. Their robes and flowers touch their bodies with the immeasurable bliss of the third dhyāna;
inner and outer radiance penetrates like a clear mirror—may I be reborn there. Defilements are ultimately extinguished through the absence of causal origination;
with immeasurable bliss, every thought-moment increases the purity of samādhi—may I be reborn there. Untainted supernormal powers, truly real and again true, bring immeasurable bliss.
Through the joy of the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*, I vow to be reborn there; May afflictions be forever severed and never again interfere, and may immeasurable bliss prevail.
In some jeweled lands, lapis lazuli is interspersed—may I vow to be reborn there; In some jeweled lands, they are formed of purple-gold—may I vow to be reborn there;
In some jeweled lands, they are made of yellow gold—may I vow to be reborn there; In some jeweled lands, they are radiant with crystal—may I vow to be reborn there; May immeasurable bliss prevail.
Some vow to be reborn in lands adorned with thousands of jewels; Some vow to be reborn where countless joys are produced by calculating jewels, each color and light reflecting one another.
Those who come from the ten directions all practice supreme, immeasurable deeds of joy;
in their dwelling, advancing, and halting, they dwell in carefree bliss—vow to be reborn there! They do not worry about official affairs nor grieve over private matters—they possess immeasurable joy.
May I be born there by making vows for spiritual transformations, whether a hundred or a thousand times, so that in every assembly I may make offerings everywhere throughout the immeasurable bliss.
Or may I be born there by creating clouds of incense and canopies of a thousand jewels, from within which clouds rain down fragrant flowers in immeasurable bliss;
may all manner of adornments emerge according to my thoughts in immeasurable bliss. Wherever I go, may wondrous marvels appear in immeasurable bliss.

May I, through the joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, vow to be reborn there; May I, until the end of my life, directly enter the assembly of the unconditioned and vow to be reborn where immeasurable bliss, jeweled trees, and jeweled groves fill every place;

May I vow to be reborn where every tree and grove is fully adorned with immeasurable bliss, their roots facing one another and their trunks looking toward each other; May I vow to be reborn where branch meets branch in symmetry and twig follows twig in harmony, abounding in immeasurable bliss.
May I be reborn there, where the joints of the stems wind around one another and the leaves follow one another in succession;
May I be reborn there, where the flowers face each other and the fruits correspond to one another, as immeasurable light of bliss shines upon both self and others’ lands;

May I be reborn there, where the radiance of that light is luminous and clear, manifesting wondrous and marvelous phenomena according to the colors of all things; All this is the power of Amitābha’s vows, creating immeasurable bliss.

May I be reborn in the jeweled stairways and paths amidst the rows of forest trees; May I be reborn amidst the infinite joy of the multi-storied pavilions interspersed throughout every realm, where celestial music resounds from layered nets;
May I be reborn to make offerings to those within the boundless pavilions, enjoying the infinite bliss of the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi*;
May I be reborn to enjoy the infinite bliss of meeting the Buddhas before my physical form withers and my life ends.
Suddenly reflecting upon that blissful vow, may I be reborn there; every person has this share—do not doubt it.
May I be reborn in the land adorned by the immeasurable joy of the vajra and the untainted, where all things clearly illuminate one another, surpassing the thousand suns.
May I be reborn in the land adorned by the power of Amitābha’s vow, where one becomes a great jewel-king of a single lotus, of immeasurable joy.

May I be reborn there, where the leaves are layered one upon another, eighty-four thousand in number; May I be reborn there, where each leaf is a mani-jewel of hundreds of thousands of billions of immeasurable joys;
May I be reborn there, where each mani-jewel radiates light of a thousand colors, shining upward to transform the void into a canopy of immeasurable joy;
May I be reborn there, where eighty thousand diamond pedestals are spread above; May I be reborn there, where nets of genuine jewels cover the flower pavilions of immeasurable joy.

May I be reborn there, where four banners support the canopy, draped with hanging cords and nets; May I be reborn there, where the body of true golden merit shines alone, enjoying immeasurable bliss, never moving from its single seat upon the lotus pedestal;
May I be reborn there, where one exhausts the limits of the future to deliver sentient beings, enjoying immeasurable bliss, universally exhorting all beings to always maintain mindfulness;
May I be reborn there, where walking, standing, sitting, and reclining cause the mind to behold immeasurable bliss.
The Buddha’s body is perfect and without blemish; I vow to be reborn there. People from the ten directions all face him directly;

I vow to be reborn there with immeasurable joy, my heart continuously turned toward him in mindfulness. With the present mind focused on the conditions before me, I shall behold immeasurable joy and the wondrous wonders of the Pure Land;
I vow to be reborn there. All this is due to the Buddha’s power bestowing its grace from afar, providing immeasurable joy.
Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta sit side by side upon a double-flower pedestal, vowing that all shall be reborn there;
each is adorned as the Buddha is, and their immeasurable bliss is like that of the four jeweled banners—may all be reborn there.

The jeweled pavilions and jeweled nets are no different [from those of the Buddha], and their immeasurable bliss is such that the three-flower pedestal stands uniquely transcendent above the assembly—may all be reborn there. The Three Bodies sit facing one another, most supreme and honored, bringing immeasurable bliss.
May the assembly of bodhisattvas from this land and other realms vow to be reborn there; may they surround [the Buddha] at all times and praise his immeasurable bliss.

May those who are like the dust motes and sands of such a great ocean vow to be reborn there. When sentient beings are born therein, they enter into immeasurable bliss that cannot be expressed in words;
may they be born there immediately. This assembly consists of those who practice exclusively with no regard for their own bodies, enjoying immeasurable bliss.
May I be reborn there where jeweled towers rise in tiers, not made by human hands; Where jeweled banners and groves of trees are likewise so;
And where immeasurable pleasure-pools and canals fill the four banks—may I be reborn there. When a gentle breeze briefly touches them, celestial music plays;
The sound of immeasurable Dharma fills my heart and pores—may I be reborn there. Therein, one immediately awakens to the gates of samādhis as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—immeasurable joy.
In each and every lotus pond, the center is filled with blossoms; may I be reborn there. Whether opening or closing, the people are countless and immeasurable;

whether sitting or standing, they call out to one another in joy; may I be reborn there. Vying to gather fragrant flowers as offerings, their immeasurable joy is such that they speak or laugh, their bodies and minds at ease;
may I be reborn there. I shall immediately remember my fellow practitioners here in Jambudvīpa; may I be reborn there in immeasurable joy.
Each shall make a vow, adding their prayers from afar for rebirth; Abide with single-minded focus without retreat, until all must come to the immeasurable bliss.
Upon arrival, one shall immediately receive the joy of purity and emptiness; I vow to be reborn there, for this purity and emptiness is the cause of Nirvana.
Immeasurable bliss reveals the nature of my mind’s recollection; I vow to be reborn there, where each person leaves half their seat for those who arrive in immeasurable bliss.

May I be born in the realm where fellow practitioners follow one another to roam the Dharma-realm; The Dharma-realm is itself the Land of the Tathāgata—may I be born there in its infinite bliss, amidst the assemblies as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in every Buddha-land.
May I be born there to hear the Dharma through emanated bodies and perform offerings, attaining infinite bliss by being graced with the compassionate light of all Buddhas.
May I be born there to receive the empowerment of the hand-touching upon my head and enter the state of non-remainder, attaining infinite bliss.

If one intends to dwell in another land, may there be the vow to be reborn there; if one desires to return, may one return immediately. Whether dwelling or returning, may there be immeasurable bliss and benefit.
May I be reborn [in that land]! In one’s own land and in other lands, there is no duality; immeasurable bliss is entirely the equal Dharma of Nirvana.
May I be reborn [in that land]! The wisdom of all Buddhas is likewise so; it is immeasurable bliss. May I be reborn [in that land]!

May I vow to be born there through the joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi; may every place be the realm of the Dharma King, and having experienced immeasurable joys through various affairs, may I return to peace and happiness—may I vow to be born there.

May I realize immeasurable dhāraṇīs and immeasurable joys together with the bodhisattvas and hosts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—may I vow to be born there. May I fill the entirety of empty space to come and make offerings, and experience immeasurable joy.

Or scattering robes and flowers that transform into canopies—may I be reborn there! Or playing music that transforms into clouds of infinite bliss, manifesting countless banners and streamers—may I be reborn there!
Within the space of a single meal, one reaches the Land of Peace and Bliss; with infinite joy and peace, the assembly of sages behold one another from afar—may I be reborn there!
Knowing them to be fellow practitioners from other lands—may I be reborn there with infinite joy!

Each arises, holding flowers to offer in worship, vowing to be born there; They are immediately led directly into Amitābha’s assembly of immeasurable bliss, where bodhisattvas from other realms join in bowing to the Buddha, vowing to be born there.
Holding flowers, they circumambulate him hundreds of thousands of times in immeasurable bliss;
Or they scatter incense and flowers while playing celestial music, vowing to be born there. Furthermore, they manifest spiritual transformations that fill the void, in immeasurable bliss.
Radiant light illuminating radiant light, making offerings to the Buddha—may I be reborn there. With one voice and in unison, they praise the immeasurable bliss of Sukhāvatī;
Amitābha moves his physical form in response to the time—may I be reborn there. The radiance of his body shines throughout the lands of the ten directions;
from that place of immeasurable bliss, he emits divine light of inexhaustible color—may I be reborn there. This returning light shines back upon the assembly of Amitābha—immeasurable bliss.
The light having finished its illumination enters through the crown of the head; may you vow to be reborn there. May the great assembly know this together:
the light of the prediction of enlightenment is immeasurable joy. Before the light has fully vanished, Amitābha smiles; may you vow to be reborn there. He proclaims to the great assembly:
"Listen with single-minded devotion! Immeasurable Joy, I now bestow upon you the prediction of Bodhi. Before long, you shall come to attain Buddhahood; this is immeasurable joy."
Those who originally dwelt in other lands and were born through transformation, now vow to be reborn here;
rejoicing in having attained this rare and marvelous Dharma of immeasurable bliss, they vow to be reborn, freed from the long eons of hardship in Saṃsāra.

Having especially received the grace of the spiritual friend Śākyamuni, and through immeasurable joy in his various skillful means of contemplation, they vow to be reborn. Having chosen the gateway of Amitābha’s great vows, they attain immeasurable bliss.
Dedicating all virtuous deeds toward rebirth is not as good as single-mindedly reciting the name of Amitābha;
with every thought of immeasurable bliss, constantly calling his name and repenting, one vows for rebirth. When people can recollect the Buddha, the Buddha likewise remembers them;

with immeasurable bliss, the ordinary and the holy know one another and their realms reflect each other, and thus one vows for rebirth. This is the supreme condition for sentient beings, bringing immeasurable bliss.
Do not believe the words of others when they pray for rebirth; simply purify the mind, and all these things will become immeasurable bliss.
If you say that this is the same as the lands of the Buddhas and pray for rebirth, then for what reason are the six realms of existence the same as birth and death?

Immeasurable suffering fills the three realms like thorns and forests; pray for rebirth. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth are all characterized by highs and lows; immeasurable suffering. Pray for rebirth.
May all sentient beings of the water, land, and empty space aspire to be born there;
Bound by the ropes of karma, craving, and delusion, they are sent to immeasurable suffering;
As the messengers of Yama drag them away, may they aspire to be born there; Driven on and on by the ox-headed jailers of hell, may they aspire to be born there. Immeasurable bliss!

May I be reborn there, where blazing fires arise simultaneously from all four directions; Blown by the winds of karma, may I fall into this place of immeasurable bliss outside the four gates of the most fiery hell (Niraya). At each gate there are eighty-four thousand partitions;

may I be reborn there, where within every single partition, person after person arrives at this place of immeasurable bliss. Within it are suffering instruments as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; may I be reborn there, where there is only immeasurable bliss.
May those whose bodies are enveloped in rising smoke and flames aspire to be born there; May those who are struck by flying wheels and swords from all directions aspire to be born there;
May those who endure immeasurable suffering within all the hells aspire to be born there; When shall we find rest in any kalpa?
May we attain the immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi and aspire to be born there; May the three evil paths be forever severed, and may we attain the nameless, immeasurable bliss.

I vow to be reborn there, amidst sevenfold iron walls and sevenfold nets; within these layered walls stand iron forest trees and immeasurable trees of bliss, their branches and twigs numbering eighty-four thousand.
I vow to be reborn there, where every leaf, flower, and fruit is like a wheel of blades;

upon immeasurable wheels of bliss, beings leap upward and then fall back down. I vow to be reborn there, where heads enter and feet emerge, a pain so unbearable it is beyond endurance. I vow to be reborn there, amidst immeasurable bliss.

Upon each successive gate, eighty thousand cauldrons boil; may I vow to be reborn there. Molten copper and iron dregs surge like springs of immeasurable joy, their surging waves rising eighty thousand fathoms high;
may I vow to be reborn there. They shoot directly out beyond the gates for a thousand yojanas;

may I vow to be reborn there. At the four gates and four paths, sinners enter into immeasurable joy; may I vow to be reborn there. When the gates open, the fires of karma come forth to welcome them into immeasurable joy; may I vow to be reborn there.
Molten iron flows and blazes, submerging one up to the knees—may I be reborn there! Smoke and flames arise simultaneously wherever one touches—may I be reborn there!
The ox-headed guardians of hell shout by the roadside—may I be reborn there! The great earth shakes like celestial thunder;
hearing this, the hearts and bellies of the sinners split asunder—may I be reborn there! Iron insects and iron birds vie with one another to devour them—may I be reborn there!
May I be reborn there, where iron balls, swords, and blades fall from the sky; Where molten copper and iron liquid are poured upon one’s body—may I attain immeasurable bliss.
May I be reborn there, forty thousand *li* from the gates of the Iron City, Where there is no place to flee as one seeks passage through the midst of it—may I attain immeasurable bliss.
May I be reborn there, where one passes swiftly like an arrow shot, swifter than the wind, Entering the sevenfold gates in an instant—may I attain immeasurable bliss.
May I be reborn in the joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, Single-mindedly recollecting the Buddha and severing greed and anger;
may I enter this gate of sevenfold iron with immeasurable joy and be reborn there. At what time and in what kalpa shall I return? May I enter with immeasurable joy;
Once the sinners have entered, the gates all close; may I be reborn there. Each individual body fills [the space] without mutual obstruction; may I be reborn there with immeasurable joy.

May I vow to be reborn there; All due to the karmic conditions of the sin of destroying the Dharma, And immeasurable joy in slandering the Triple Gem and ruining the virtuous vows of others, may I vow to be reborn there;
Also falling into the great Avīci Hell, And immeasurable joy in playing and laughing while committing sins for many kalpas, may I vow to be reborn there;
Not cherishing the Buddha’s intent but grasping at human sentiment, may I vow to be reborn there.
Be careful not to let a frivolous mind run wild with the three karmas; vow to be reborn there. The paths of karma are distinct and cannot be deceived;
vow to be reborn in the immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi. Crossing directly through the paths of karma to enter the Western Land;

vow to be reborn in the immeasurable bliss beyond the gates of the sevenfold iron city. Iron pythons raise their heads as they emerge from atop the city walls; vow to be reborn in the immeasurable bliss.
May they be reborn there, as tongues of flame and wheels of swords issue from the mouths [of the guardians], all of which pour down upon the sinners;
may they be reborn there, where immeasurable bliss flows through the pores of the iron dogs at the four corners; may they be reborn there, where smoke and fire rain down upon the bodies of men;
may they be reborn there, where rākṣasas brandish spears and pierce the heart-eyes; for it is solely because of the heart-eye that one falls into the hells—may they find immeasurable bliss.
Upon the ground of glowing red-hot iron, there is endless suffering; may I be reborn [in that land]. Whether the sinner lies down or walks about, there is immeasurable joy;
when the great kalpa comes to an end, they see it with their own eyes—may I be reborn [in that land]. Outside the eastern gate of the city, there are pure forests and springs of immeasurable joy;
the sinner suddenly turns toward the east and runs—may I be reborn [in that land]. Just as one is about to reach the gate, it closes again—there is immeasurable joy.

Thus, at these four gates, for half an eon, I vow to be reborn there. With iron nets hooking their bodies like thorny forests, though they have immeasurable suffering, may I be reborn above, where vultures peck at human flesh.
Upon the ground, copper dogs compete to devour them; though they have immeasurable suffering, may I be reborn there.
On the ground and in the void, there is no place of refuge; As soon as they move, the instruments of torture multiply even more; though they have immeasurable suffering, may I be reborn there.
Pray for rebirth in the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi; Hearing this teaching, my heart is shattered with sorrow—how immeasurable is my joy in praying for rebirth!
Disrespectful toward parents and reviling the Triple Gem, I pray for rebirth; At the end of life, the fires of hell will come to meet me—how immeasurable is my joy in praying for rebirth!
Having brought shame upon my kin and violated the pure precepts, I pray for rebirth; I shall likewise fall into such a niraya—how immeasurable is my joy in praying for rebirth!
Those who kill sentient beings and eat the flesh of others, yet vow to be reborn here— They shall enter directly into the mass of flames of hell;
O Infinite Joy, see and hear this skillful means! Those who kill for the sake of their livelihood, yet vow to be reborn here— They shall suffer as before for an incalculable time; O Infinite Joy!
Those who steal the property of the Triple Gem or the belongings of sentient beings, yet vow to be reborn here— Once fallen into hell, there will be no time of escape; O Infinite Joy!
Those who steal from or plunder the property of their parents and six relations vow to be reborn there; they shall likewise enter such hells of immeasurable bliss.
Those who do not spare their own bodies or wealth but constantly practice dedicated giving vow to be reborn there; they shall enjoy immeasurable bliss.

Those who defile the pure conduct of teachers and monks through evil attachments vow to be reborn there; they shall remain in hell for eternal kalpas with no hope of escape, yet experience immeasurable bliss.

May those sentient beings who are perversely defiled and their retinues be reborn here; may they find immeasurable bliss, for otherwise they would surely enter hell and suffer for immeasurable kalpas.

If one obtains a human body, may there be the bliss of being free from the retribution of being a eunuch; may one find immeasurable bliss, for otherwise one’s six kin would dwell together like enemies.

May one find immeasurable bliss in the bliss of the *pratyutpanna-samādhi* (Banzhou Sanmei); may one vow to sever perverse thoughts and cultivate pure conduct (*brahmacarya*). May one find immeasurable bliss.
May those sentient beings who have deceived the Triple Gem be reborn here; Having died, they enter the hells with no time of escape—may they be reborn here.
Those who delight in immeasurable evil speech, double-tongued slander, greed, hatred, and pride; Who pervade the eighty thousand hells—may they be reborn here.
Those who delight in immeasurably speaking of the faults of others regarding the Triple Gem; Having died, they enter the hell of the plucked tongue—may they be reborn here.

I universally exhort all sentient beings to protect their three karmas and vow to be reborn there; whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, they shall mindfully recite the name of Amitābha at all times.
In the midst of infinite bliss, they shall constantly remember the hells and vow to be reborn there;

they shall arouse the supreme aspiration for rebirth and vow to never commit karma that leads to the three miserable realms. Even toward the joyful rewards of humans and devas, they shall have no attachment, remaining within infinite bliss.

Suddenly remembering the long-lasting suffering of the hells, I vow to be reborn there; Never forsaking even for a moment, I forget worldly ease for the sake of immeasurable bliss—the land of the Buddha of Peace and Bliss, the realm of the unconditioned—I vow to be reborn there. To bring ultimate peace to my body is truly the essence:
the immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi—I vow to be reborn there. Only the single path of the Buddha is uniquely pure and tranquil—immeasurable bliss.
The adornments of the Pure Land are inexhaustible; I vow to be born there. Those born from the ten directions are likewise infinite and immeasurable;
for thousands of kalpas, ten thousand kalpas, and kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, I vow to be born there. All who depart do not obstruct one another; there is immeasurable joy.
The sentient beings of the ten directions have never decreased; I vow to be born there. In the land of Amitābha Buddha, there is also no increase; there is immeasurable joy.
By the power of Amitābha’s vows, may I be reborn according to my great aspiration for immeasurable bliss;
May I be reborn with the four kinds of adornments pervading everywhere, and with the constant mastery of the three knowledges and six supernormal powers for immeasurable bliss;

May I be reborn by universally entering the thoughts and minds of sentient beings, and by the Buddha’s body and marks arising in accordance with the mind for immeasurable bliss; May I be reborn so that upon mere recollection, the True Gold Buddha appears, for immeasurable bliss.
Pure gold is the very form of Amitābha; I vow to be reborn there. The circular halo manifests transformation-buddhas before one’s eyes;
with immeasurable bliss and countless marks and signs, I vow to be reborn through the eighty-four thousand vows. Each and every ray of light illuminates the ten directions;
with immeasurable bliss, may light shine universally without other distractions—I vow to be reborn there. Seeking only those who recite the Buddha's name for rebirth, there is immeasurable bliss.
All myriad practices turn back together; may I attain the vow to be reborn there. The single practice of mindfulness of the Buddha is most supreme;

the various good deeds of immeasurable joy may lack sufficient power—may I attain the vow to be reborn there. For no more than one day or seven days of mindfulness, when life is about to end, the Holy Assembly shall appear—may I attain the vow to be reborn there.
Immediately seated upon a lotus pedestal, I shall reach the Land of Jewels and its immeasurable bliss.
In the pure great ocean, may all those who have made vows be reborn; seeing those born from afar, all rejoice immeasurably.
May I be reborn with no difference from the Buddha of Immeasurable Joy, whose voice and marks are sublime. Compassionately rescuing those in suffering, he is most powerful;
may I be reborn in the joy of the *apramāṇa* and the joy of the *pratyutpanna-samādhi*. Not transgressing the teacher’s instruction, one contemplates Amitābha; this is immeasurable joy.
Though the rescue from suffering is distant across another world, I vow to be reborn there; When sentient beings cry out in urgency, you come at that very moment—endless bliss.
Appearing in the forms of śrāvakas or bodhisattvas according to conditions, you joyfully deliver sentient beings—endless bliss.
With a compassionate heart you uproot suffering and transcend the three realms—endless bliss. With a loving heart you bestow happiness and aim for nirvāṇa—endless bliss.
