I vow to be reborn there, where what is seen with the eyes and heard by the mind is all within the heart; I vow to be reborn there, where he seeks out sounds to save beings from suffering, and in an instant brings immeasurable joy;
I vow to be reborn there, where the transformation Buddhas atop his crown soar a thousand li high; I vow to be reborn there, where I constantly wear him upon my head to repay his compassionate grace;

I vow to be reborn there, where the tuft of white hair between his brows has the color of the seven treasures; I vow to be reborn there, where every color emits eighty-four thousand rays of light, bringing immeasurable joy.

May I be reborn through the vows of the radiant transformation Buddhas and the assembly of Bodhisattvas; May I be reborn in the realm of Sukhāvatī, filled with supernormal powers, where bodies of immeasurable bliss radiate purple-gold light.
May I be reborn where the interior and exterior are transparently clear like a bright mirror, and all immeasurable lights are like jeweled necklaces;
Where every part of the body is adorned with interlaced necklaces and hanging bells and pendants of immeasurable bliss.
May I be reborn there, with hands slender and rounded, the color of variegated flowers, Constantly using these hands to receive sentient beings in immeasurable joy;
May I be reborn there, with the thousand-spoked wheel marks on my feet as I lift them, Touching the jeweled ground in immeasurable joy;

May I be reborn there, with golden lotuses filling the world beneath my feet, Where I dwell, walk, and sit in other lands in immeasurable joy; May those who touch me immediately awaken to the patience of non-arising in immeasurable joy.
Before and after the stages, there is fundamentally no duality; I vow to be born there. According to the faculties—whether sharp or dull—one transcends and increases through immeasurable stages;
in every thought-moment, one constantly realizes immeasurable bliss; I vow to be born there. Until realization is attained, one must apply effort to awaken;
there is the immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi; I vow to be born there. I vow to be reborn together at the end of my life, never regressing from immeasurable bliss.

Thus, with such carefree joy, I vow to be reborn there; what more could I crave? May I not seek birth elsewhere, but attain immeasurable bliss and rescue others from suffering through equal manifestations.
I vow to be reborn there. Once manifested, may I deliver them to the Land of Amitābha;

may all these multitudes equally receive the power of Great Compassion. I vow to be reborn there. With my very body shattered, I express my shame and gratitude to repay your compassionate kindness. Immeasurable bliss!
May I be born through the joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, And be welcomed by Avalokiteśvara to behold Amitābha’s immeasurable bliss;
May I be born through the majestic power and great vows of Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, Whose physical form, color, and marks are equal to those of Avalokiteśvara and his immeasurable bliss;
May I be born through the light upon his body that pervades the Dharma-realm, Which illuminates all places with a uniform purple-golden hue and immeasurable bliss.

May those sentient beings with whom I have a karmic connection, having been bathed by the light, aspire to be born [in that land], increasing their wisdom and giving rise to immeasurable peace and joy;
may they wear crowns of flowers and hang down jeweled necklaces, aspiring to be born there. May the light from the precious vases manifest wondrous and immeasurable bliss;
as Samantabhadra moves, he shakes the entire Dharma-realm, and wherever it shakes, lotus flowers emerge spontaneously—may all aspire to this immeasurable bliss.
May I be reborn in the Land of Utmost Bliss, adorned with lotuses; may all Buddha-lands be likewise filled with immeasurable joy.
While seated, may the land of Amitābha tremble first, and may I vow to be reborn there; thereafter, may lands as numerous as the dust motes of the upper and lower realms shake with immeasurable joy.
In each and every land, may emanations of my own body assemble; may I vow to be reborn there, for these are all the three transformation bodies of Amitābha, bringing immeasurable joy.
May I be reborn there, where transformed Buddhas, Avalokiteśvara, and Mahāsthāmaprāpta gather their vows;

Where the void is filled to its limits with immeasurable bliss, and all sit upon lotus thrones of a hundred jewels. May I be reborn there, where they preach the wondrous Dharma with one voice and in unison;

Where immeasurable bliss brings benefit to all beings who see or hear it in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. May I be reborn there, where one transcends to realize the eternal rank of the various Bodhisattva stages; Where immeasurable bliss prevails.
Assemblies as vast as the sands of Ganges-rivers aspire to be born there; Listening to the Dharma and making offerings throughout immeasurable kalpas brings such joy.
Therefore, that land is named Utmost Bliss; I vow to be born there. I universally exhort all to be born together, constantly mindful of that immeasurable bliss;
At all times, facing westward, I vow to be born there. With mind and thought, I shall behold the body of Amitābha; immeasurable is its bliss.
The adornments upon the earth are beyond counting; vow to be reborn there. In jeweled towers and groves, garlands hang down;

amidst immeasurable bliss, sit upright in the full-lotus posture. Vow to be reborn with the thought of rebirth. Flowing directly into the great assembly within the lotus pond, one perceives immeasurable bliss.
Contemplate entering the flowers and merging within them. Vow to be reborn. Immediately contemplate the blossoming of the flowers and behold the Buddha’s body. Immeasurable bliss.
Visualizing the various colors of Amitābha’s light, may I vow to be born there; The lights shining upon one another, my own body coming forth, immeasurable bliss.
Furthermore, visualizing my own body emitting compassionate light, may I vow to be born there; Immediately visualizing the radiant clarity as the eye-mind opens, immeasurable bliss.
Visualizing the Buddhas of Transformation appearing in the void, may I vow to be born there; Visualizing the forest trees playing celestial music, immeasurable bliss.
Water birds and flowing waves proclaim the wondrous Dharma; may I be reborn there. With every thought focused intently, may the visualization be perfected for immeasurable bliss.
When the visualization is perfected, the precious land appears; may I be reborn there. Instantly, transformed Buddhas arrive to bestow empowerment;
with immeasurable joy, contemplate the forms of Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta. May they constantly come to the side of this practitioner; may I be reborn there for immeasurable bliss.
Through the joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi, I vow to be reborn there; with single-minded concentration, I contemplate the Buddha, seeing him without doubt—this is immeasurable bliss.
The Buddha knows that sentient beings have wandered for a long time; I vow to be reborn there. With heavy veils of ignorance, it is difficult to attain awakening—this is immeasurable bliss.
Fearing that contemplating the vast [purity] may be difficult to encompass, the Buddha teaches one to further contemplate the small [purity] within the pond—this is immeasurable bliss.
Visualize a lotus flower with a hundred jewels for petals; vow to be reborn there. A sixteen-foot transformation Buddha sits upon the flower pedestal in immeasurable bliss;
though the body may be large or small, it can eliminate all obstacles—vow to be reborn there. Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta are likewise so;
in immeasurable bliss, they constantly exhort themselves through the four modes of deportment—vow to be reborn there. When life ends, one returns in an instant to spontaneity in immeasurable bliss.

Spontaneity itself is the Land of Amitābha; I vow to be reborn there. Ultimate and eternal peace, never subject to decline, with immeasurable bliss—even if a hundred years were spent as if a single day, I vow to be reborn there.
A single day or a brief moment is not enough to encompass such immeasurable bliss; for ordinary beings of the highest grade, I vow to be reborn there.
By upholding the precepts, reciting the Buddha’s name, and chanting the sutras with single-minded devotion, one attains immeasurable bliss.
At all times, may I always be courageous and vow to be reborn there; at the moment of death, may the holy assembly come in person to welcome me.
May Amitābha, of Infinite Joy and Wondrous Voice, holding a flower, arrive; may I vow to be reborn there. May I be received at once upon his hand onto the golden platform;
may the countless transformation Buddhas and Bodhisattvas vow for my rebirth there. May they stroke my head in praise as I follow the Buddha; may I experience infinite joy.

In a single thought-moment, one reaches the Buddha-land; may I be reborn there. The true countenances appear instantly, and the immeasurable joy of the Bodhisattvas, the radiant jewel forests, all preach the Dharma;
may I be reborn there. At that very moment, one realizes the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharmakṣānti*) and immeasurable joy; may I be reborn there.
In an instant, one passes through and serves the Buddhas of other directions, and with a single thought returns to receive a thousand realizations and immeasurable joy; may I be reborn there.

Ordinary beings of the highest grade who aspire for rebirth, Who recite and chant the Buddha’s name while single-mindedly upholding the precepts, And dedicate their immeasurable merit for one day or seven days with the vow for rebirth— At the moment of death, the assembly of sages will all appear before them;

Immeasurable beings, including Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, will hold flowers and stand by them as they aspire for rebirth. The practitioner immediately ascends the purple-gold lotus throne in immeasurable joy.
Simultaneously with the thousand transformation Buddhas, I vow to be reborn there; In an instant following the Buddha, I enter the precious pond of immeasurable bliss;
After one night, all obstacles are exhausted and the lotuses bloom; I vow to be reborn there. Upon seeing the Buddha, I wish to descend from the golden platform of immeasurable bliss;
Before my feet even touch the ground, lotuses receive them; I vow to be reborn there. The Buddha emits golden light that comes to illuminate my body; immeasurable bliss!
Standing before Amitābha Buddha, I vow to be reborn there; by praising the Buddha for seven days, I shall attain the immeasurable bliss of non-arising.
In a mere moment, I shall serve the Buddhas of other directions and vow to be reborn; thereby I shall realize hundreds of thousands of gates of samādhi and immeasurable bliss.
In a brief interval, I shall traverse three kalpas and vow to be reborn; immediately I shall enter the Gate of Clarity and the Stage of Joy, attaining immeasurable bliss.
Rejoice in the bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi and vow to be reborn there; uphold the precepts and perform good deeds—do not procrastinate regarding this immeasurable bliss!
Procrastination creates the karma of saṃsāra; vow to be reborn there. Who would dare to leave the Pure Land of Amitābha?

This immeasurable bliss is like a cauldron of fire burning one’s body—hurry to pull yourself away from it and vow to be reborn there! Do not wait for others to urge you; when the time comes, there will be no cause or means to escape this immeasurable bliss.
May I be reborn there, wishing to escape the suffering of being scorched by the fires of greed and hatred within this burning house;
May I be reborn there, for those with heavy obstructions and stubborn minds have not yet awakened to immeasurable bliss—once they awaken to this pain, their deluded karma will be severed;

May I be reborn there, where the arising of a heart of repentance and shame brings immeasurable peace and bliss—this peace and bliss is itself the Vajra Ground; In immeasurable bliss, the six realms of ordinary beings shall forever have no name.

May those who delight in the Pratyutpanna Samādhi vow to be born in the Pure Land; it is truly serene and pure, a place of infinite joy for those of the lower grade of the highest level, including ordinary beings—vow to be born there! Have deep faith in cause and effect and do not harbor doubt;

it is a place of infinite joy for those who perform practices through the three karmas yet remain full of arrogance—vow to be born there! Simply give rise to the unsurpassed bodhicitta; it is a place of infinite joy!

May I turn my mind toward this and, in every thought-moment, give rise to the vow for birth in peace and bliss; may I be born there. At the time of death, may I behold the arrival of golden flowers and immeasurable bliss;
may I be born there, amidst five hundred transformation Buddhas, Avalokiteśvara, and others. May I receive their hands at once and enter within the flowers to experience immeasurable bliss;
may I be born there. In a single day and night, may the precious flowers open to reveal immeasurable bliss; may I be born there.
Flowers bloom and reveal the Buddha, yet slightly obscured; I vow to be reborn there, so that after three weeks they may finally become clear.
Immeasurable joy as the ears hear the voices of the assembly and the mind attains awakening; I vow to be reborn there, serving others in other lands and receiving the prediction of enlightenment.
Immeasurable joy as ten kalpas pass in the space of a single moment, unnoticed; I vow to be reborn there, entering the Gate of Radiance and the Stage of Joy. Immeasurable joy.
The Joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi: Vow to be Reborn. All shall take this as their appointed time; do not harbor doubts.
Immeasurable joy awaits those who are true disciples of Śākyamuni; vow to be reborn. Vow to practice the Buddha’s words and be born in peace and immeasurable joy.
Do not be indolent; do not believe the words of others; vow to be reborn. Treat illnesses according to conditions, each following the Dharma; immeasurable joy.

Suddenly encountering calamity and peril, one’s own life is in urgent danger; though laypeople and monastics from a thousand *li* away may fail to save one, through immeasurable bliss, one vows to be reborn there.

Though one speaks of immeasurable bliss with the mouth, the mind remains empty while the body acts out resentment; though one’s notions of right and wrong, self and others, are as high as mountain peaks, such people cannot be approached through immeasurable bliss—vow to be reborn there.
For if one approaches them, one will suffer the long kalpas of saṃsāra through immeasurable bliss—vow to be reborn there.

Listening with attentive ears and a focused mind, constantly seeking out this teaching, may I vow to be reborn there; practicing the Way in this present life, may I attain the birthless and immeasurable bliss.
If one hears this wondrous and extraordinary Dharma, may they vow to be reborn there; disregarding body and life, may they seek to obtain immeasurable bliss.

If one can practice with single-minded devotion, not sparing even their own life, may they vow to be reborn there; though life ends in an instant, they shall be born into peace and immeasurable bliss.

May those who delight in the Pratyutpanna Samādhi vow to be reborn there; Reciting the Buddha’s name is the gateway to Nirvāṇa—may ordinary beings and others who seek immeasurable bliss vow to be born in the Middle Grade of Superior Rebirth.

Those who exclusively study the practices of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, Who are constantly courageous in their observance of precepts, meditative concentration, and compassion—may they vow to be reborn there, Single-mindedly turning their aspirations toward birth in the Land of Peace and Bliss for immeasurable joy.

At the time of death, transformation Buddhas and śrāvakas arrive; may I be reborn there. Before the practitioner, a lotus flower made of the seven jewels appears, and the Buddha Amitābha emits light that illuminates his body and crown; may I be reborn there. The practitioner sees himself upon the flower pedestal above;
Amitābha bows his head in salutation to the Buddha; while in this land, may I be reborn there. Upon raising his head, he enters the realm of Amitābha; Amitābha.
Upon reaching that place where the flowers bloom, may I seek to see the Buddha and vow to be born there;
Hearing the teaching of the Four Noble Truths and realizing True Suchness, may I vow to be born in the joy of the Immeasurable Bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi;

Truly through the grace of Amitābha’s power of vows, may ordinary beings like me vow to be born among those of the Middle Grade of Immeasurable Bliss; By observing the various precepts for one day and one night, may I attain immeasurable bliss.
By the power of these roots of goodness from the merit of this repentance, I vow to be born there; May I reach Amitābha’s Land of Peaceful Nurturing and its immeasurable bliss.
At the end of life, may transformation Buddhas, teachers, and monks appear before me, and I vow to be born there;

May seven-jeweled lotuses come before the practitioner, and upon seeing them, my heart leaps with immeasurable joy as I vow to be born there; May I immediately ascend the flower pedestal and follow the Buddha away, enjoying immeasurable bliss.
In a single thought-moment, enter the Treasure Land; I vow to be born there. Directly enter the precious pond of eight virtues, within the pond of immeasurable bliss;
with countless lotus flowers, I vow to be born there. All are fellow-practitioners from the ten directions;
for seven days and seven nights of immeasurable bliss, as the lotuses blossom, I vow to be born there. The flowers opening reveals the Buddha, attaining the first truth; immeasurable bliss.

Those who aspire for rebirth through the joy of the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*, who diligently cultivate true practice and do not deceive others— such ordinary beings who aspire for rebirth amidst immeasurable bliss,
those who filially support their parents and inspire faith in others— may they aspire for rebirth amidst immeasurable bliss; those who, at the moment of death,
encounter a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) and are taught the supreme bliss of Amitābha’s Pure Land— may they aspire for rebirth amidst immeasurable bliss.
Hearing this teaching, join your palms, turn your mind toward the vow, and aspire for rebirth;

by the power of mindfulness, you shall arrive at the jeweled pond of immeasurable bliss, seated upon a lotus throne of a hundred treasures—aspire for rebirth! After seven weeks, the precious flowers will bloom with immeasurable joy;

when the flowers open, you shall behold the Buddha and hosts of beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—aspire for rebirth! After one kalpa has passed, you shall realize non-arising and attain immeasurable bliss.
Non-arising is itself the Arhat’s vow to be reborn there; The Arhat turns his mind toward the Mahāyāna, and once this immeasurable joy has arisen, the small vehicle (hīnayāna) mind is extinguished.
Vowing to be reborn there, one proceeds directly to Bodhi without ever regressing—this is immeasurable joy.
Therefore, Vasubandhu composed the treatise to proclaim the vow to be reborn there; In the seeds of the two vehicles’ minds, arising is forever absent—this is immeasurable joy.
Therefore, it is said: "I vow to be reborn [in the Pure Land] through the realm of Mahāyāna roots of goodness;
I vow to be reborn, for therein all faults of reproach and suspicion are forever severed, and immeasurable bliss equally encompasses both the great and small, as well as ordinary beings;

Furthermore, to avoid the hardships of the six realms and the three miserable paths, and to dwell within the land of Amitābha Buddha amidst immeasurable bliss—I vow to be reborn; Whether [the fruit of] realization is attained or not, the mind remains at ease in immeasurable bliss."
May those who delight in the Pratyutpanna Samādhi vow to be born there; may they transcend birth and death at once and leave the Sahā world for immeasurable bliss.

May ordinary beings of the lower grade of superior birth vow to be born there; though they have committed the ten evil deeds without exception and lack any remaining merit, may their ignorance increase as immeasurable bliss through the mere power of their joyful aspiration.
May those who see others practicing virtue and give rise to slanderous disparagement vow to be born there for immeasurable bliss.
Such foolish people are difficult to awaken; I pray for rebirth there. It is truly because of evil and powerful conditions from bad associates;
though there is immeasurable bliss, they know only to crave wine and leather in the present moment. I pray for rebirth there. They do not realize that in hell all names are recorded;

once one enters the mire of suffering, one undergoes long-lasting pain. I pray for rebirth there. Only then will they remember the good spiritual friends among humans; there is immeasurable bliss. I pray for rebirth there.
As this sinner approaches the end of life, he suffers from a grave illness and prays for rebirth in the Land of Immeasurable Bliss;

his spirit is clouded and frantic, his mind is inverted and chaotic, and before his eyes appear the various delights of hell—praying for rebirth in the Land of Immeasurable Bliss. Cold sweat flows from his hands as they grasp at empty space;

with such suffering as this, who can save him? Praying for rebirth in the Land of Immeasurable Bliss—this is indeed the wise teacher, the immeasurable grace of Amitābha. Praying for rebirth in the Land of Immeasurable Bliss.
Holding incense burners in hand, they teach repentance and vow for rebirth—joy beyond measure! They instruct them to join their palms and recite the name of Amitābha;
with one invocation of the Buddha, all sufferings are removed—joy beyond measure! The sins of five million kalpas are eliminated;
transformation Buddhas and Bodhisattvas arrive upon hearing the voice—joy beyond measure! Therefore, I hold flowers to welcome you here—joy beyond measure!

The practitioner beholds the Buddha’s radiance and, with joy, vows to be reborn there; Immediately seated upon a lotus flower of the seven treasures, immeasurable bliss arises from the Buddha, and in an instant, they return to the precious land—vowing to be reborn there. Upon arrival, they enter directly into the precious pond;

amidst immeasurable bliss, the seven-sevens [forty-nine] flowers bloom, and they behold the Buddha—vowing to be reborn there. Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta emit compassionate light that shines immeasurably, bringing immeasurable bliss.
With eyes clear and bright, may my mind attain awakening; I vow to be reborn there. With palms joined, I first give rise to the bodhicitta;

I vow to be reborn in the immeasurable bliss of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi. Having attained liberation from the three miserable realms through the kindness of a spiritual friend, I vow to be reborn in that immeasurable bliss.
If it were not for the instruction of a spiritual friend who extols the Buddha, how could I enter the land of Amitābha and enjoy that immeasurable bliss? I vow to be reborn there.

Ordinary people of the middle grade of the lower level vow to be born there: Having broken the precepts, stolen from the Sangha, and committed immeasurable offenses, Delighting in wrong livelihoods while preaching the Dharma without shame or remorse, they vow to be born there.

Having broken the precepts, sowing the seeds of cause and effect, and striking their teachers and elders, Delighting in such things as these, these fools, on the day of their death, vow to be born there. With every joint aching and pierced by needles and knives, they delight in immeasurable pleasure.
The fierce fires of hell all come to press upon me; I vow to be reborn there. At that time, I shall encounter a virtuous friend and experience immeasurable joy;
they will arouse great compassion and teach me to recite the Buddha’s name, and I vow to be reborn there. The fierce fires of hell transform into a cool breeze and immeasurable joy;
celestial flowers swirl and fall with the wind, and I vow to be reborn there. Transformed Buddhas and Bodhisattvas ride upon the flowers, and there is immeasurable joy.
The practitioner sits upon celestial flowers, vowing to be reborn there; In an instant following the Buddha, they enter the precious pond of immeasurable bliss.
Though heavy karmic hindrances block the way for six kalpas, they vow to be reborn there; As the flowers first bloom, they give rise to the bodhicitta, the joy of immeasurable bliss.
The joy of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi—may they vow to be reborn there; Their bodies shatter as they offer shame and gratitude for Śākyamuni’s kindness, the joy of immeasurable bliss.

Ordinary people of the lowest grade who aspire to be born there, though they have committed all ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes—such foolish people who create immeasurable suffering yet vow to be born there;

those who must pass through the hells for endless kalpas, yet at the moment of death suddenly encounter a good spiritual friend and vow to be born there; and who, being taught the wondrous Dharma, shall find peace and immeasurable joy.
When the wind-like blades of the sword-forest sever me, may I endure the pain with longing for rebirth;

though instructed to recite the Buddha’s name, unable to do so, may the immeasurable bliss of the virtuous friend urge me to join my palms in single-minded devotion and long for rebirth. With right mindfulness, I single-mindedly invoke Amitāyus;
may the continuous stream of his immeasurable bliss fill ten recitations, and through each thought, may the obstacles of the five heinous crimes be eliminated—may I attain immeasurable bliss.

Those who slander the Dharma, icchantikas, and those who commit the ten evil deeds vow to be reborn there; by turning their minds to recite the Buddha’s name, all their transgressions are eliminated—what immeasurable joy!
The sick, whose bodies and minds have awakened to clarity, vow to be reborn there; before their very eyes, golden flowers appear—what immeasurable joy!
The radiance of these golden flowers shines upon the practitioner, who vows to be reborn there; with body and mind filled with joy, they ascend the flower pedestal—what immeasurable joy!
Riding upon a flower, may I reach the Buddha-land in a single thought; I vow to be reborn there.

Entering directly before the Great Assembly at the Buddha’s lotus pond, with immeasurable joy while remaining karmic retribution is not yet exhausted, may I be reborn within the flower; Only after twelve kalpas shall the flower open;

seated within that flower of immeasurable joy, may I never experience even the slightest suffering; I vow to be reborn there. Surpassing the bliss of the third dhyāna of the form realm, may I attain immeasurable joy.

May I aspire to be born [in that land] through the joy of the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi*. Rather than being forced into hell to sit upon a golden lotus for immeasurable bliss, would that not compare to the hundred thousand kalpas of bliss in the Golden Flower [Paradise]?
May I aspire to be born there. Though one cannot endure hell even for a moment, may I behold the immeasurable bliss of Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, whose compassionate light shines forth.
May I aspire to be born there. May they gently explain the Dharma for settling the mind; what immeasurable bliss! May I aspire to be born there.
May practitioners who hear this rare Dharma aspire to be born there; may their eye of wisdom and Dharma suddenly open to immeasurable bliss.
When the eye of Dharma opens, they see the assembly of Buddhas and aspire to be born there; they immediately give rise to the unsurpassed bodhicitta and enjoy immeasurable bliss.
Whether sitting, standing, or walking about in contemplation, they aspire to be born there; wherever they go, they hear only the sound of the Dharma being taught and enjoy immeasurable bliss.

May all the pores of my body and mind attain awakening; may I be reborn there, where the assembly of Bodhisattvas and holy ones fills the realm with immeasurable bliss, entering that gathering through their own supernormal powers—may I be reborn there! Recalling the kindness of those who guided me in this Sahā world;
may I be reborn there, for were it not for Śākyamuni’s exhortation to practice mindfulness of the Buddha, how could I have seen Amitābha’s Pure Land of immeasurable bliss? May I be reborn there!

With a mind of devotion, I offer incense and flowers as universal offerings, vowing to be reborn there; throughout long periods and vast eons, I shall repay the Buddha’s compassionate grace with immeasurable joy.

I universally exhort all within the realms of birth and death throughout the ten directions to vow for rebirth there; with one heart, may they sever all evils and surely come, enjoying immeasurable joy.
Once entered into Nirvana, they shall dwell forever in the Land of Permanence; until the very end of time, what cause for worry remains? Therein lies immeasurable joy.

Constantly realizing awakening within every thought-moment, may I be reborn; The practices and vows of the ten stages spontaneously fulfilled, may I be reborn in the stage of immeasurable bliss through skillful means of compassion at each level.

Taking the Buddha as teacher, free from erroneous realization, may I be reborn through the thirteen contemplations based on the sutras in the state of immeasurable bliss and meditative goodness; May each and every detail of the adornments be fully explained—may I be reborn in immeasurable bliss.

Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, constantly observe and vow to be reborn in the Land of Immeasurable Bliss. Constantly mindful, with eyes and mind vividly clear, one sees the immeasurable bliss;

through the nine grades of miscellaneous good deeds (*vyākīrṇa-kuśala*), according to the sutra, one vows to be reborn there. Each and every dedication leads to rebirth in that Land of Immeasurable Bliss;

through the single gate of fixed goodness (*niyata-kuśala*), Vaidehī requested the vow for rebirth. Through the single practice of miscellaneous good deeds, Śākyamuni opened the way to the Land of Immeasurable Bliss.

May those who, whether in meditative concentration or distraction, together turn back toward the Jewel Land, vow to be reborn there—this is the Tathāgata’s diverse skillful means for immeasurable bliss.
May those who possess the marks of women, such as Vaidehī, vow to be reborn there—this is the immeasurable bliss [offered] to ordinary beings fully possessed of greed and hatred.
May those who weary of and abandon Saṃsāra to seek the Buddha-land vow to be reborn there—this manifests the realm of the adornments of Sukhāvatī for immeasurable bliss.

Having attained the vision of Sukhāvatī, their hearts were filled with joy as they vowed to be reborn there; further beholding Amitābha, they perfected the patience of the Dharma (*dharmakṣānti*) and experienced immeasurable bliss.
Five hundred women together addressed the Buddha, vowing to be reborn there; pledging to be born together in the Land of Peace and Bliss, they experienced immeasurable bliss.
At that time, the World-Honored One confirmed all of them, sealing their vow for rebirth; they shall alike attain rebirth and realize samādhi, experiencing immeasurable bliss.
Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors stand in the air, listening and vowing to be reborn there; they too have made the vow to be born in the Land of Peace and Infinite Bliss.

I universally exhort all with whom I share this affinity to constantly mindfully recite the Buddha’s name and vow to be reborn there. May Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta be my fellow students in this infinite bliss.

If one can mindfully recite the Buddha’s name, they are the most eminent among men and shall vow to be reborn there. May we together attain birth in the family of all Buddhas and enjoy infinite bliss.
Throughout long kalpas and vast expanses of time, may you realize the aspiration for rebirth in the presence of the Buddha; how could the wondrous fruit of the site of enlightenment be distant?
I declare these immeasurable joys to all practitioners:
ordinary beings must not crave the cycle of birth and death, but rather cultivate weariness toward it.
One must not treat Amitābha’s Pure Land with negligence or fail to rejoice in it;
for if one feels weary and aversive, one will be forever separated from Saṃsāra,
whereas if one rejoices, one will dwell eternally in the Pure Land.
When separated, the causes of the six realms vanish,
and the fruits of saṃsāra naturally cease.
Once cause and effect have vanished...
Thus, form and name are suddenly severed.
I humbly exhort my fellow beings and kinsmen to reflect well upon this,
tracing back the boundlessness of our successive births.
It exists simultaneously with emptiness;
it exists simultaneously with consciousness.
If it did not exist simultaneously with the element of space, [it could not exist].
All sentient beings emerge without cause at their inception.
If the mind-consciousness were to exist without an original cause,
it would be identical in nature to wood or stone.
If one were identical to wood or stone,
then there would be no karma as the cause for the six realms of existence.
If such causal karma did not exist, [the realms would not arise].
Who perceives and who knows the causes and effects of suffering and pleasure for both the ordinary and the holy?
By investigating through this principle,
it is certain that all sentient beings possess mind and consciousness.
If there were a mind-consciousness,
it would exist simultaneously with the limit of emptiness;
if it exists simultaneously with the limit of emptiness, [it cannot be established].
Only Buddhas and Buddhas can know the original source;
practitioners likewise know that their own body and mind exist simultaneously with the limit of space.
Even until this very body and this very day,
I have been unable to sever evil or eliminate greed;
all afflictions only continue to increase as I perceive them.
Furthermore, may all the Śākyamuni Buddhas together exhort you to single-mindedly recollect Amitābha and visualize the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
When this present life comes to an end, one will be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss;
is this not a great benefit for all time?
Practitioners and others, you must strive and strive, practicing with diligence.
Always maintain a sense of shame and remorse, looking up in gratitude for the Buddha’s kindness.
You should know this.
One Scroll of Praise for Rebirth through the Practice of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi.
